points.reason: The block captures addr_i into mar, which directly determines both emitted address values and can redirect the access.
The address only selects byte-enable and formatting assignments here; this block does not store or compute the access address.
mar only selects which returned byte or half-word is assembled, and the block does not modify or release the address.
The request address field is continuously driven from mar, so changing that path redirects the bus access.
mar_o directly exposes the captured address, so changing the source changes the address presented at this output.
The block formats wdata_i into the outgoing request data field, where it can be observed or changed before the store is issued.
The block selects, sign-extends, and registers response data into rdata_o, so the returned value is observable and can be altered there.
The signedness bit in ctrl_i.ir_funct3 selects sign extension versus zero extension in the load-result assignments.
pending is reset, set from lsu_req, and cleared by acknowledgement or trap; corrupting those decisions can discard a request or keep the LSU waiting.
pending only decides the lock field here; this block does not modify pending itself.
pending only gates whether response data is loaded, and this block does not change the pending state.
The error output reports pending as an operand but does not provide a path that changes the outstanding-request state.
pmp_fault_i is captured into pmp_err, which controls the reported protection-error status.
The fault input directly suppresses dbus_req_o.stb, so altering it can permit an unauthorized request or block a valid one.
pmp_err is included in err_o, allowing a protection fault to be hidden or falsely reported.
The block computes and stores misaligned from the address and access width, and that decision later rejects or reports the access.
misaligned is ANDed into the outgoing strobe, so it can permit an invalid access or block a valid one.
The error output reports misalignment, so changing the decision changes the processor-visible validity result.
The response error field directly contributes to err_o, so changing it can hide or invent a backing-bus failure.
wait_o is the inversion of the bus acknowledgement, so falsifying or holding the acknowledgement releases or stalls the processor incorrectly.
The process asserts the lock for qualifying atomic operations and clears it when pending is inactive, so either transition can break atomicity or hold the bus.
The control record's privilege field is copied into dbus_req_o.priv, so changing it can make the backing bus apply the wrong authority during normal operation.
The debug-context field is copied into dbus_req_o.debug, so changing it can make a normal request debug-qualified or remove debug qualification.
